Rep. Mejia Denounces Swastika Discovered at Millburn Library | Representative Analilia Mejia Skip to main content Rep. Mejia Denounces Swastika Discovered at Millburn Library June 26, 2026 Press Release Millburn, NJ – Today, Rep. Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) released the following statement denouncing the swastika discovered at Millburn Library: “I am deeply disturbed that a swastika was discovered at the Millburn Public Library. This hateful act of antisemitism must be unequivocally condemned. Hate has no place in our community. Acts like these do not occur in a vacuum. Antisemitism has been rising across this country for years—in our schools, in our public spaces, in the texture of daily life. What happened in Millburn is part of that story and we must reject it. In moments like this, we do not get to look away. It takes all of us to stand against antisemitism and ensure our neighbors feel safe, welcome, and supported. That’s why I have co-sponsored the Antisemitism Response and Prevention Act and the Holocaust Education and Antisemitism Lessons (HEAL) Act, supported resolutions recognizing the contributions of Jewish Americans and condemning antisemitism, and will continue to stand with our Jewish neighbors. I commend Mayor Saccomandi, Millburn Township, and the Millburn Police Department for their swift response. My office stands ready to support any member of our community..” ### Media Press Releases In the News Back to top button

Rep. Mejia and Rep. Ramirez's $25 Minimum Wage Bill Introduced in the Senate | Representative Analilia Mejia Skip to main content Rep. Mejia and Rep. Ramirez's $25 Minimum Wage Bill Introduced in the Senate June 25, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON D.C. – This week, the Living Wage For All Act , co-lead by Rep. Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) and Rep. Delia Ramirez (IL-03) in the House of Representatives, was introduced in the U.S. Senate by U.S. Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.)  to increase the federal minimum wage to 25 an hour. Under a two-track phase-in, large corporate employers would be required to implement a $25 wage floor by 2032, while other businesses would have until 2039 to do so. The bill would also guarantee a living wage for workers by mandating automatic, continued increases of the federal minimum wage to two-thirds of the national median wage. The bill   is cosponsored by  U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) ,  Andy Kim (D-N.J.) , and  Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) . Despite widespread gains in worker productivity, alongside stark rises in the cost of living, Congress has not increased the federal minimum wage since the first Obama administration. Since 1979, workers have become some 92 percent  more productive, but wages have risen by less than 34 percent. If the minimum wage had kept pace with inflation and worker productivity since 1968, it would have been roughly $25 in 2023. There is nowhere in America  where a worker with just one dependent can afford their basic needs by working full time at an hourly wage under $25. As low wages put families in a financial chokehold, local businesses lose out from a diminished customer base, and our broader national economy misses out on substantial gains in employee engagement and reductions in staff turnover. While many states and localities have increased their minimum wages with consistently positive results for workers, in twenty states the minimum wage still does not exceed the federal floor established nearly two decades ago. Statement From Rep. Mejia on the Death of Edwin Jeovanny López Cornejo at Delaney Hall | Representative Analilia Mejia Skip to main content Statement From Rep. Mejia on the Death of Edwin Jeovanny López Cornejo at Delaney Hall August 4, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Representative Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) released the following statement after confirmation that Edwin Jovanny López Cornejo, a 39-year-old father detained at Delaney Hall, died in ICE custody this past weekend: “Edwin Jovanny López Cornejo, a father who made a life here for 20 years, is dead, and my gravest concerns about conditions for medically vulnerable people at Delaney Hall are now confirmed. Edwin’s family has serious concerns about the medical treatment he received in detention, and I share those concerns,” said Congresswoman Analilia Mejia. “This is not the first life we’ve lost inside that facility. New Jersey’s own health inspectors have been denied full access, including the medical unit, again and again. If there’s nothing to hide, there’s no reason to keep them out. DHS must carry out a full, independent investigation. This family, and New Jersey, deserve real answers, justice, and accountability. Under these conditions, medically vulnerable people are being given death sentences due to the lack of care. Delaney Hall must be shut down. Abolishing and replacing ICE is the only way to correct this—a system that lets this happen again and again cannot be reformed. It must be rebuilt around human dignity.” ###   Mejia Press | Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ11) 1427 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC  20515 Media Press Releases In the News Back to top button

Rep. Mejia Convenes Voting Rights Forum Marking 158th Anniversary of the 14th Amendment | Representative Analilia Mejia Skip to main content Rep. Mejia Convenes Voting Rights Forum Marking 158th Anniversary of the 14th Amendment July 13, 2026 Press Release Legal experts, civil rights advocates, and community leaders joined the Congresswoman to discuss threats to equal protection and the freedom to vote MONTCLAIR, NJ — Today, Rep. Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) hosted "Defending Democracy: The 14th Amendment and Voting Rights Act Forum" at Montclair State University, bringing together legal experts, civil rights advocates, and community members to mark the 158th anniversary of the 14th Amendment's ratification and examine growing threats to equal protection, due process, and the right to vote. Rep. Mejia and panelists traced the 158-year arc of the 14th Amendment, from its roots in the fight for voting rights to the landmark rulings on marriage equality and bodily autonomy it helped make possible. That progress now faces real threats, from the Supreme Court's rollback of key Voting Rights Act protections to new legislation like the SAVE America Act aimed at making it harder to register and vote. The conversation dug into how we arrived at this moment, what is genuinely at risk for everyday New Jerseyans right now, and the concrete steps advocates, courts, and lawmakers must take to rebuild and defend the amendment for the next 158 years. The forum comes as Rep. Mejia leads the Defend the 14th Amendment Task Force alongside House Democrats, a coalition she launched this week to push back against efforts to weaken constitutional protections for equal protection, due process, and citizenship. “So many Americans don't realize how much of their daily lives are shaped by the 14th Amendment, from the right to vote to the right to marry who you love, the right to citizenship by birth, and the right to make decisions about your own body. These protections were not handed to us. We fought for them, amendment by amendment, ruling by ruling, and we can lose them the same way if we stop paying attention. Congresswoman Mejia, Leader Jeffries Hold Roundtable on Inhumane ICE Detention at Delaney Hall | Representative Analilia Mejia Skip to main content Congresswoman Mejia, Leader Jeffries Hold Roundtable on Inhumane ICE Detention at Delaney Hall August 11, 2026 Press Release For Immediate Release: August 11, 2026 Contact: Beth Wiesinger | NJ11AMPress@Mail.House.Gov MORRISTOWN, NJ – Today, Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) was joined by House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (NY-08) and Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08) at Calvary Baptist Church in Morristown for a private roundtable with families affected by the Trump administration's immigration detention policies. Participants included former detainees and family members of current detainees at Delaney Hall and Elizabeth Detention Center; the families of Jean Wilson Brutus and Edwin Jovanny López Cornejo, both of whom died in ICE custody; Reverend Samaria Tillman and Reverend Jerry Carter Jr. of Calvary Baptist Church; Morristown Mayor Tim Dougherty; and Morris Township Mayor Donna Guariglia. Families described conditions inside Delaney Hall and the Elizabeth Detention Center, focusing on the treatment of medically vulnerable people in ICE custody. Participants described facility staff withholding medication or administering it at incorrect doses, ignoring requests for medical attention, and inflicting a toll on their households and families that has lasted long after detention ended. Several described ICE agents taking them into custody without warning during routine activities, ignoring their legal status, and holding them for weeks before release. Leader Jeffries, Congresswoman Mejia, and Congressman Menendez discussed congressional efforts to strengthen oversight of ICE detention facilities and hold the agency accountable for conditions inside them. "Today, I sat with families who have lived through something no family should ever have to endure. Their grief is real, and so is their bravery in choosing to share it with us today," said Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11). Congresswoman Analilia Mejia Marks First 100 Days in Congress with Bold Action for NJ-11 Families | Representative Analilia Mejia Skip to main content Congresswoman Analilia Mejia Marks First 100 Days in Congress with Bold Action for NJ-11 Families July 29, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) today marked her first 100 days in Congress, a period defined by robust legislative action, sustained oversight of the Trump administration, and direct engagement with constituents across New Jersey's 11th District. In her first week in office, Representative Mejia introduced her first bill, the Living Wage for All Act. The legislation raises the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour and has since been introduced in the Senate. Since then, she has co-sponsored 85 pieces of legislation, including Medicare for All, the College for All Act, and the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, along with measures to reform the Supreme Court, guarantee universal child care and paid leave, overturn Citizens United, protect LGBTQ+ rights, enact tax fairness, lower housing and energy costs, and support parents and caregivers. In the district, Rep. Mejia recently secured more than $5 million in federal grants from the Department of Health and Human Services for health care and child care programs. She has held two town halls to hear directly from constituents and, as a member of the House Small Business Committee, has visited local business owners across the district while voting to invest greater resources in Main Street. "My first 100 days have been about carrying our district with me into every room I walk into down in Washington, D.C., from Randolph to Belleville and everywhere in between," said Congresswoman Analilia Mejia . "When I introduced a bill to raise the minimum wage to $25 an hour, I was thinking about families working multiple jobs just to keep up. When I launched the 14th Amendment Task Force, I was thinking about our neighbors whose rights and safety are under threat.
